goal: Decide what the merge controller does to keep a stacked pull request mergeable, so a merged base never strands the pull requests stacked on it.

app.name: uor-stack-step
app.title: Stack step
app.purpose: Decide whether the controller retargets, updates, escalates or leaves one open pull request, from what its base branch is and what GitHub reports about merging it.

fields.name: base
fields.means: the base branch is the default branch, the head of a pull request that has merged, or the head of one still open

fields.name: mergeable
fields.means: GitHub's mergeable state: mergeable, behind a base a strict ruleset requires it to contain, conflicting, or not yet computed

meanings.retarget: the base is set to the merged pull request's own base, which already contains the old base's commits through its merge commit
meanings.update: GitHub's update-branch merges the base into the head
meanings.escalate: the pull request is labeled needs-rebase and an agent-task issue names it, for the scheduled agent loop to resolve
meanings.wait: nothing is done until GitHub has computed the state

rules.why: GitHub Docs, Changing the base branch of a pull request; git-merge(1): a merge commit keeps the old base an ancestor, so the stacked head stays a descendant and conflicts with nothing
GitHub Docs, Resolving a merge conflict: a conflict needs a change to the head, which only an author can make
GitHub REST, Get a pull request: mergeable is computed in the background and is null until it is
GitHub REST, Update a pull request branch: merges the base into the head when the head is behind

app.otherwiseWhy: a clean pull request on a live base needs nothing

properties.why: no pull request stays on a merged base
a clean pull request never asks an agent for work
